title: Runtime low-bit operational playbook: hybrid kernel constraints and KV coherence
body:
Purpose and audience

This playbook describes pragmatic runtime constraints, scheduling rules, and KV cache coherence patterns for shipping low-bit execution paths (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) in the serving runtime. It is intended for runtime engineers, kernel maintainers, and release engineers preparing canaries or dedicated pools that allow mixed-precision models. This is intentionally operational — focused on behaviors the platform must guarantee and checks we should run during rollout.

Scope and guarantees

- Scope: forward path kernels (attention, MLP, layernorm, rotary/alibi), KV cache semantics, request scheduling, memory/DMA constraints, correctness guardrails for model fidelity when using quantized kernels. Does not cover offline quantization tooling or model conversion caveats in detail.
- Hard guarantees: determinism of KV lookups within a request, no cross-request KV leakage, fallback-to-higher-precision for correctness-critical tokens (see fallback policy), and observable metrics that correlate bitwidth choices with perplexity/regression signals.

Assumptions and platform constraints

1) Hardware: targets are recent NVIDIA Ampere+ and equivalent accelerator backends that expose int8/float8 kernels. Memory copy windows are constrained (max contiguous pinned host buffer per op = 256MB).
2) Kernel implementations vary: some kernels (AWQ/GPTQ) only implement fused MLP kernels; others provide separate GEMM and quant-dequant steps. Runtime must detect capability via capability tags returned at startup.
3) Model variants: customers may pin model to a quantized-only variant or allow runtime to substitute quantized variants for cost-focused routing.

Kernel capability metadata (runtime-discovered tags)

Each worker advertises a flat capability list (strings). Examples:
- bitwidth:int8
- bitwidth:fp8
- quant:awq:fused-mlp
- quant:gptq:per-channel
- kernel:kv-fused
- op:rotary:fp8-safe

These should be treated as booleans by the scheduler. Absence of a tag implies unsupported.

Operator constraints and safe patterns

- Attention: prefer kernels that preserve exact KV layout (no hidden reordering) for sharded KV. If only a quantized attention kernel exists that reorders KV for cache efficiency, mark that worker as kv-reorder:allowed and limit such workers to non-eviction-critical routes.
- MLP: fused AWQ/GPTQ MLP is acceptable when per-layer reconstruction error budgets are satisfied in offline eval (see test plan). If fused kernel does not support certain activation shapes, runtime must split MLP per-block and use dequantize->float path for those blocks.
- Layernorm and norm-adjacent ops: if quant kernels are not numerically stable (observed drift > threshold), prefer FP16/FP32 for those layers. Runtime should expose per-layer precision overrides in model config.

KV cache coherence and sharding rules

- Affinity: assign an incoming conversational session to a single KV-holding worker to avoid cross-worker coherence. Sticky assignment TTL configurable per-route (default 30s).
- KV serialization format: canonical format must include (layer_id, beam_id, token_index, dtype_tag) so workers with mixed bitwidths can safely reconstruct.
- Hot-prefix reuse: when a worker supports in-place quantized KV (no dequantize), allow re-use; otherwise, runtime must reconstruct dequantized KV to serve subsequent requests.
- Eviction policy: when evicting quantized KV shards, prefer evicting float variants first to preserve quantized cached tokens if the route is sensitive to latency.

Fallback and correctness-first heuristics

- Token-level fallback: if a quantized kernel produces logits with outlier confidence (z-score above 8 compared to FP baseline for top-1), re-run that token (or next token generation) on a float-safe path. Record as a replay metric.
- Sequence-level rollback: if a short sequence (<= 8 tokens) shows cumulative probability delta > epsilon (runtime-configurable) vs baseline, trigger a per-request fallback for remaining generation to the higher-precision variant.

Scheduling rules and prioritization

- Priority tiers:
  - tier-0: latency-sensitive routes (default to float-safe kernels if fidelity unknown)
  - tier-1: cost-optimized routes (prefer quantized kernels; allow aggressive batching)
  - tier-2: background/off-peak (max parallel batching)
- Batching windows: quant kernels often tolerate longer batch windows; default batch time for tier-1 is 8ms, tier-0 is 3ms. These values should be dynamically tuned per-model.
- Kernel selection algorithm (per-request):
  1) resolve model config precision hints (per-layer overrides)
  2) check worker capabilities
  3) if worker supports requested kernel, schedule; else determine if safe fallback exists locally (e.g., split-block fallback)
  4) if not local, consult routing policy to route to compatible worker pool or enqueue for float path depending on SLA

Memory and DMA operational constraints

- Workgroups must limit pinned host buffers. If a single request's dequantized intermediate would exceed the per-op host buffer limit, fail fast and signal to caller with retriable=false and suggested action: reduce request length or use dedicated capacity.
- For FP8 kernels requiring staging buffers for per-channel scales, pre-allocate scale buffers at pool initialization to avoid runtime malloc stalls.

Telemetry and observability

Instrument the following metrics per model/route/worker:
- quant_kernel_calls_total (labels: quant_type, op, worker_id)
- quant_replays_total (why: token-fallback, shape-mismatch, numeric-outlier)
- avg_fidelity_delta (observed token logit delta aggregated against an FP baseline sample set)
- kv_hit_ratio_by_dtype (labels: int8, fp8, float16)
- worker_capability_gauge (bitwidth tags present)

Testing and rollout checklist

1) Offline: per-layer reconstruction error matrices for each quant variant on representative prompts (synth + customer workload). Thresholds: mean logit delta < 0.03, top-1 mismatch < 0.6% for non-critical routes.
2) Unit: kernel-level unit tests for shapes, fused/unfused codepaths, and multi-batch behavior. Include malformed-shape fuzzing.
3) Integration: end-to-end test that simulates KV shard handoff, eviction and hot-prefix reuse with mixed bitwidth workers.
4) Canary: small % traffic to quant pool with 5-minute anomaly detection for perplexity drift and token-replay spikes.
5) Gradual roll: 5% -> 25% -> 100% by route with rollback autopilot on fidelity regressions.

Operational runbook (short)

- Detect: increase in quant_replays_total, spike in avg_fidelity_delta or sudden drop in kv_hit_ratio_by_dtype.
- Mitigate: disable quant routing for affected route (flip route policy to float-safe), scale up float-safe pool, or increase token-fallback aggressiveness (lower threshold to force earlier replays).
- Post-mortem: ingest sample request traces (token-by-token logits) and run offline comparison tool to identify failing layer/kernels.

Open questions and next steps

- Per-layer on-the-fly switching cost: should we allow dynamic intra-request precision switching per-layer to minimize fallbacks? Need perf study.
- Operator fusion safety: establish a minimal correctness test that any fused kernel must pass before being advertised as fused-mlp:safe.
- KV format evolution: consider compact delta-encoded KV for long histories to trade compute for memory.

Appendix: quick config knobs

- route.precision_preference = [cost|fidelity|balanced]
- worker.capability_tags = [comma-list] (populated at agent startup)
- kvcache.sticky_ttl_ms = 30000
- quant.fidelity_threshold = 0.03
- quant.token_fallback_z = 8

Notes and references

This playbook should be paired with the low-bit test harness (linked above) and the kernel API spec. The next revision will propose canonical KV serialization and an automated fuzz suite for mixed-precision KV exchanges.

Authorship and context

Drafted by Priya Shah (serving runtime lead) with input from runtime and applied-ml. Intended as an operational bridge between kernel authors and runtime schedulers — practical rules to lower rollout friction while keeping customers safe.
